extracted.intended_audience: writers of narrative nonfiction (journalists, creative-nonfiction authors, reporters)
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and evaluative criteria for crafting narrative nonfiction: choosing the right narrative form and structure, shaping scenes, character, voice, POV, reporting, and ethical practice so material reads as a true story with causal arc, stakes, and resolution rather than an essay or sketch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match form to material
rubrics_metrics.description: Many writers force material into the wrong shape. Story narrative requires: a protagonist; a complication; a resolution; a meaningful change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the material lacks a protagonist, complication, resolution, or meaningful change, it belongs in a different form (explanatory, profile, personal essay). The primary test is whether the material can be told as a story (with arc) rather than only as an essay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure — selecting the right narrative shape
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose the narrative structure that fits the material rather than imposing a shape on unsuitable material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hart emphasizes assessing whether material supports a full dramatic arc (story narrative) or should instead be treated as explanatory narrative, profile, personal piece, or anecdote; select structure accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of View — POV choices in nonfiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Make deliberate choices about point of view appropriate to nonfiction material and ethical constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: POV choices affect how much interiority, distance, and authority are granted; select and maintain a coherent POV that serves clarity, accuracy, and the reader's experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice and style — voice-finding; style as honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a voice appropriate to the subject; treat style as an expression of honesty rather than ornament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice should reflect truthful engagement with material; style choices should serve clarity and ethical presentation rather than mask or dramatize facts improperly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character — real people on the page
rubrics_metrics.description: Portray real people as characters—fully realized, behaviorally-drawn persons—while respecting factual accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use scenes, action, and dialogue to reveal character rather than summary; balance vividness with ethical obligations to truth and attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene — the basic unit of narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Use scenes as the primary building blocks of narrative rather than relying on summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scenes should dramatize events in time and place, show actions and reactions, and advance causality and conflict; avoid turning scenes into mere recap or exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action — what happens, dramatized
rubrics_metrics.description: Dramatize what happens—show actions and their consequences rather than merely reporting them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action should be concrete and causal, helping to build rising action and push toward a turning point and resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue — capturing real speech
rubrics_metrics.description: Capture real speech in dialogue that sounds authentic while remaining accurate and attributable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dialogue should reveal character and advance scene/action; in nonfiction, take care to report dialogue faithfully and note reconstruction or paraphrase where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme — what the story is 'about'
rubrics_metrics.description: Be clear about what the story is 'about'—the underlying idea or question the narrative explores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theme should emerge from the action and resolution rather than being imposed didactically; the ending should illuminate the theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting — information-gathering for narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Undertake thorough reporting to provide the factual foundation for scenes, dialogue, character detail, and causal claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Robust reporting supplies the specific details that make scenes credible; accuracy, attribution, and verification are part of craft as well as ethics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story narratives — full dramatic arcs
rubrics_metrics.description: Story narratives should present a full dramatic arc (protagonist, complication, rising action, turning point, resolution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use causality, conflict, stakes, rising action, and resolution to structure the arc; ensure the ending registers meaningful change and offers insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory narratives — story as essay
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize explanatory narratives where the material is principally about explanation or idea rather than dramatic change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When material is better suited to exposition, structure it as explanatory narrative or essay rather than forcing it into a story shape that would be untrue to the material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other narratives — personal, profile, anecdote
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate among other narrative forms—personal essay, profile, anecdote—and use the form that best fits the material and purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each form has different expectations for voice, POV, use of scenes, and relation to truth claims; do not conflate forms just because they are narrative-adjacent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics — truth, accuracy, attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain truth, accuracy, and proper attribution as core ethical obligations in narrative nonfiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical practice governs how scenes, dialogue, and reconstructed moments are handled; be transparent about reconstructions and protect subjects from misrepresentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story-Power — causality
rubrics_metrics.description: Causality: events linked by cause-and-effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A convincing narrative ties events through believable causal chains; avoid implying causation where only coincidence exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story-Power — conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflict: protagonist vs. obstacle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conflict provides the engine of interest and drives rising action; identify and dramatize the obstacle the protagonist faces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story-Power — stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakes: something matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear what is at risk for the protagonist so readers understand why events matter; stakes can be personal, social, moral, material, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story-Power — rising action
rubrics_metrics.description: Rising action: escalation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange scenes and events to escalate tension and complication toward a turning point; avoid static or episodic sequences that do not build.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story-Power — resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolution: change + meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ending should show a meaningful change and illuminate the significance of events; resolution need not be tidy but should register consequence and insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality test — can material be told as a story (with arc) or only as an essay?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the material supports a story-shaped arc or is better presented as essay/explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a first-order filter before attempting a narrative: if no protagonist/conflict/turning point/resolution exist, consider other forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality test — does the protagonist face a real obstacle?
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that the protagonist confronts a genuine obstacle that fuels conflict and action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 'obstacle' is trivial or only interpretive, the piece may not sustain a story narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality test — is there a turning point?
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for a turning point that changes the direction or stakes of the narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A turning point is necessary to move from rising action to resolution; without it, the story may feel episodic or unresolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality test — does the ending illuminate?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the ending sheds light on meaning, consequences, or change rather than merely stopping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endings should illuminate theme or consequence; an ending that doesn't clarify why the story mattered suggests a weak resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality test — are scenes scenes (not summaries)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure scenes function as scenes—dramatic, time-and-place units that show action—rather than generalized summaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If much of the piece summarizes rather than dramatizes, it likely lacks the immediacy and causal clarity of strong narrative nonfiction.
